subject: Executive Brief: MercuryPay reserved throughput shortfall — GPU pool saturation and customer impact
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Prioym Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: MercuryPay: reserved throughput shortfall — immediate attention

Team,

Heads up — MercuryPay (MP-2025-38) is reporting sustained latency > 1.2s P95 on their reserved capacity endpoints and a spike in 429/503s over the last 45 minutes. Their ops channel just posted multiple traces showing request queueing against the dedicated GPU pool.

Quick facts pulled from the alert:
- Customer tier: Reserved (monthly commit)
- Reserved throughput: 22k tokens/min sustained (~367 tps equivalent)
- Observed behavior: steady token backlog, increased reject rate to 6.8% for model-redwood-7b-q4 on the dedicated pool, tail latency P95 ~1.2s -> 2.1s on some calls
- First alert: 2027-05-20T12:20:00Z (approx)

I attached a telemetry snapshot we pulled and flagged the relevant Grafana dashboard (link below). We need a short exec-ready summary and an ask:
1) Immediate customer-facing remediation and timeline (CS)
2) Emergency engineering mitigation plan + ETA to restore headroom to SLA (Infra/SRE)
3) Approval route for temporary reserved-capacity burst (cost owner / finance)

Marissa — can you confirm what MercuryPay is seeing on their side (they indicated production customer-facing errors) and whether leadership is on this?
Prioym / Rishi — propose options and fastest safe path to restore their throughput. If we need to expand the dedicated pool or migrate them temporarily to a hosted variant, call it out with an estimate.

On time pressure here — MercuryPay is close to a renewal window and this is high-visibility.

Thanks,
Mike
Michael Grant
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

I'll be the primary customer contact; I recommend we provide a one-paragraph exec summary (who/what/impact/ETA) and a technical remediation message for Elena.

Quick technical summary and immediate mitigation options:

Root cause hypothesis (initial): scheduling pressure on the dedicated GPU pool serving MercuryPay (model-redwood-7b-q4); continuous batching combined with long-running KV-cache-heavy requests is producing uneven headroom and queue growth for short-duration bursty requests. We see queue length climb on Pool-ID: dp-9c4b.

Options (fastest -> slower):
A) Emergency headroom rebalance (5–10 minutes): temporarily increase pool worker count by 2x for dp-9c4b and limit batch window for their customer route to 8ms. Risk: short-lived capacity contention for other Dedicated customers. Requires exec approval for temporary reserved burst.
B) Route MercuryPay chat endpoints to hosted variant (15–20 minutes): create a traffic rule to send 20%–60% of chat traffic to hosted-redwood-7b-q4-fallback. Pros: low-risk; cons: possible cost and slightly different latency profile.
C) Apply per-customer adaptive batching and KV-cache pinning (1–2 hours): safer, reduces token cost long-term.

Immediate actions I'll run on approval:
- Trigger runbook: Emergency capacity scaling (https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/emergency_capacity_scaling)
- Execute: increase pool target (internal command) and apply routing rule
- Validate with Grafana (link below) and share telemetry snapshot to customer

ETA estimates: A) ~10–20 minutes to see headroom improvement; B) ~20 minutes to full effect; C) longer.

I'll queue the change for A) pending cost approval; otherwise we'll start B) immediately.

Prioym
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MercuryPay: reserved throughput shortfall — immediate attention

Cost/impact note and request for expedited approval:

If we do option A (temporary doubling of dp-9c4b), estimated incremental cost for the 24-hour window is ~USD 6.4k (GPU hours + cross-region egress buffer if we add capacity in another region). Option B (hosted fallback) has lower direct infra cost but increases per-token bill for MercuryPay (we can absorb per-sales decision) and may add ~USD 3.5k/day in episodic hosting spend depending on traffic split.

Operational constraints: the emergency scaling action is quick but requires a sign-off from an exec cost owner (Sales ops + Finance) and an engineering lead to run the manual scale (I can lead the run but need permission). I'm attaching a short cost estimate.

Risk callouts:
- If we scale dp-9c4b, there is a transient increase in GC/slot occupancy which could create brief elevated latency for unrelated customers; our SLOs allow for a brief maintenance window but we should communicate proactively.
- If we route user traffic to hosted variant, we must ensure no PII flows violate their data controls; Marissa, please confirm.

Proposed immediate plan (recommended):
1) Approve Option A for a 6-hour temporary burst while we apply Option C permanently.
2) Notify MercuryPay leadership with ETA: 30 minutes for visible improvement, 2 hours for stable behavior.

Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

- Impact: ~10–15% error rate on invoice/chat flows; business impact visible to customer leadership.

- Timeline: visible improvement in ~30 minutes after scale, stable state in ~2 hours.

If approved, Prioym will execute and Rishi will validate. Marissa will issue a customer-facing note with timeline.

Please reply with APPROVE or DENY. If APPROVE, include any fiscal constraints (charge to deal MP-2025-38 / Opex).

Thanks — need fast response: customer leadership is asking for an immediate remediation.

Mike
